kind: Independent acceptance review, reconciled with final local evidence

criteria.assertion: Loopback test with many delayed matches: cancel after the first pending response, observe a final FE00 and no newly generated matches after cancellation is processed.
criteria.rationale: Five delayed matches with deterministic checkpoints: before-first yields FE00 immediately; midstream sends one pending then FE00; completion race sends five pending then exactly one FE00. Real ServerSession loopback; independent captured command parsing confirms statuses. CLI/Workshop controlled outcomes are supplementary, not proof they originated a C-CANCEL.

criteria.assertion: Cancellation of a different message ID does not cancel the active request; subsequent legal association use remains possible.
criteria.rationale: Wrong message ID and wrong presentation context are ignored. Both original and reused message ID requests return five matches plus success; intervening C-ECHO succeeds after late cancel.

criteria.assertion: Allow already-sent/in-flight pending responses before FE00; do not assert instantaneous zero additional bytes.
criteria.rationale: Tests allow previously transmitted pending responses and assert the no-new-match boundary only after a deterministic post-send checkpoint and processed cancellation. They do not require instantaneous absence of all in-flight bytes.

criteria.assertion: Use a delayed Storage SCP and several instances; cancel mid-transfer, then verify FE00, no further initiated stores, and exact completed/failed/warning counts.
criteria.rationale: Independent delayed Storage SCP receives only three of five requested stores in the mixed case. After cancellation, in-flight third store settles, FE00 reports completed 1 / failed 1 / warning 1; no fourth store starts. Silent destination deadline reports one failed attempted store and association reuse succeeds.

criteria.assertion: If Remaining is included, it equals sub-operations not initiated due to cancellation.
criteria.rationale: Captured FE00 Remaining is 5 before any store, 2 after three initiated stores, 0 after all five. Mixed completed/failed/warning counters sum to the three initiated stores.

criteria.assertion: Mix successful/warning/failed stores before cancellation and verify counter classes and Failed SOP Instance UID List rules.
criteria.rationale: Mixed responses success/B000/A700 yield completed 1 / warning 1 / failed 1. Failed SOP Instance UID List contains only 2.25.401.1.3 and no Specific Character Set. All-completed cancellation has no failure identifier.

criteria.assertion: OPTIONS at the configured service base with supported Accept returns 200 and a parseable, structurally conforming capabilities payload.
criteria.rationale: Configured base paths produce 200 JSON/XML WADL. JSON structure and XML/JSON method parity checked. Saved XML independently validates against pinned official WADL XSD with local XML schema catalog; schema_validation.status=passed.

criteria.assertion: Check advertised resource methods against implemented handlers and test content negotiation/error responses.
criteria.rationale: Every advertised method is checked against routing; every advertised GET and declared response media type is executed with synthetic storage/UPS fixtures. UPS create/update response contracts are exercised. HTTP negotiation/error cases cover weighting, exclusions, charset, invalid query/body and method.

criteria.assertion: A browser CORS preflight remains valid without swallowing a standard capabilities request.
criteria.rationale: CORS preflight is 204 with allow headers and no body; ordinary Origin-bearing OPTIONS capabilities request remains 200 with negotiated payload.

criteria.assertion: For each advertised true retrieval capability, execute a minimal valid request against an appropriate fixture and verify it is implemented.
criteria.rationale: All 16 advertised GET targets are asserted in the focused fixture test, including each retrieval route/media type. Six external HTTP dataset/metadata retrieval routes return 200; CLI study/series/instance downloads equal fixture bytes.

criteria.assertion: With the current unsupported bulk-data handler, both private and standard capability views disclose it as unavailable.
criteria.rationale: Unsupported bulk/rendered/thumbnail/frame handlers return 501. Standard WADL omits those resource capabilities; both private capability views declare bulkdata=false and rendered=false.

criteria.assertion: Implementing bulk data later requires real payload/media-type acceptance cases before changing the capability flag.
criteria.rationale: Condition not triggered: M4 does not implement bulk-data retrieval and keeps the capability unavailable. Retain this criterion as a mandatory future gate: real bulk payload and media-type acceptance cases must pass before advertising support. This is neither an executed pass nor a waiver.

criteria.assertion: Store a synthetic instance, stop the process, restart with the same data directory and configured durable mode: FIND locates it and GET/MOVE retrieve the same SOP identity.
criteria.rationale: Real dicom-server process stores a synthetic instance, terminates/restarts in filesystem mode, and CLI FIND/GET/MOVE recover the same SOP identity and exact dataset hash. FIND also succeeds after SIGKILL/restart. Three Workshop ViewModel routes succeed against restarted server. Process restart durability only; no power-loss qualification.

criteria.assertion: Reindex handles duplicate SOP UIDs and unreadable/corrupt files deterministically with visible errors; it does not silently claim a complete index.
criteria.rationale: Fresh executable startup visibly refuses duplicate UID, corrupt/truncated/trailing-garbage/unreadable files and symlinks. Focused tests verify no usable partial index, idempotent identical retransmission, conflict preservation and missing indexed file errors.

criteria.assertion: If durable SQLite is unavailable, startup clearly refuses that mode or explicitly selects volatile behavior; PostgreSQL help and error behavior agree.
criteria.rationale: Default durable mode is explicitly filesystem reindex. SQLite and PostgreSQL command/backend URL modes refuse startup with clear diagnostics; help names them unimplemented and points to filesystem. This refusal is only AC03 evidence: AC01 independently establishes actual durable reindex behavior.

packaged_gui.independent_visual_review: Six saved screenshots visually inspected for expected ERROR/SUCCESS status and available FE00/count/retrieval output; first empty-FIND case verified from full AX snapshot. AX deltas may omit retained text; no whole-console byte-equality claim.

skip_accounting.note: Initial counts concern XCTest only. Swift Testing contributes 89 Web and 142 Studio passes. The later 8-method CLI rerun adds 2 unique passes and repeats 6; three opt-in XCTest harness methods execute separately. All five initial skips now have explicit passing runs. Regular unique focused total is 512; opt-in 3 and Python audit 30 are additional, distinct counts.

source_integrity.repair_provenance: Final manifest supersedes the earlier pre-repair freeze. Final macOS alias/realpath StorageManager repair + test preceded server 101-pass rerun; PostgreSQL CLI/URL diagnostic expectation repair preceded durability 20-case rerun. Final CI ordering/support edits are included in this manifest.

limits: Synthetic local loopback fixtures only; external PACS interoperability is not established.
Controlled CLI/Workshop FE00 campaigns validate outcome presentation; real server cancellation is established by separate ServerCancellationTests.

DICOMStudio ViewModel runtime evidence is distinct from the seven packaged-app GUI actions and seven final CLI replays. Saved screenshots/AX, request identifiers and retrieved file hashes were independently reviewed. No user cancel button was added; controlled FE00 responses exercise client presentation.
Capabilities HTTP transport is a test adapter calling the real Swift request handler; no production HTTP listener was added.
No bulk-data implementation or successful bulk payload acceptance is claimed; NET-09-B-AC03 remains a future mandatory condition.
Durability covers completed stores and process SIGTERM/SIGKILL restart, not power-loss or every storage/filesystem fault.
No additional build, product edit, documentation edit or ledger edit was performed by this review.
